held.title: The Salt Oracle
held.reason: genre question: seventeen years after the internet crashed, a floating college in the Baltic and an oracle tradition (Locus, FanFiAddict); unclear whether it is post-collapse SF (which leaf) or fantasy

held.title: A Granite Silence
held.reason: scope question: Historical Novel Society calls it her first historical novel (1934 Aberdeen child murder); BSFA-shortlisted, speculative element unconfirmed - SFF or exclude?

held.title: HIM
held.reason: genre question: Jesus born biologically female and identifying as male, a retelling of the Gospels (Locus: 'alternative history'; New Scientist calls it science fiction). No religious-retelling leaf; SF or Fantasy under the magic rule?

held.title: Notes from a Regicide
held.reason: no clean leaf: New York a thousand years ahead, a trans man reads the memoir of his late adoptive parents' revolutionary past (PW 'dystopian', Reactor). Social science fiction sits under Modern day; Futurist dystopia leaves don't fit a family memoir.

held.title: Once Was Willem
held.reason: no clean leaf: dark fantasy in 12th-century England during the Anarchy, a monster who was once a village man (PW, Locus). No 12th-century period leaf (Autumn Kingdoms is 14th c.) and the monster angle is Supernatural, which is frozen.

held.title: Slow Gods
held.reason: no confident leaf: deep-space SF (New Scientist, Kirkus) about Mawukana, a remade 'poor copy' of himself, and a planet doomed by a collapsing binary star. Candidates Future history in space or Hard Conceptual SF; reviews don't settle it.

held.title: The City in Glass
held.reason: leaf question: an immortal demon's love for her invented city Azril, which angels destroy (Library Journal, Locus). Invented-world demon fantasy; no Fantasy Realms leaf fits.

held.title: The Siege of Burning Grass
held.reason: leaf question: SF war novel of two rival powers and a captured pacifist (Reactor, Ancillary Review). No clear leaf; Future war is thin on fit and the setting reads secondary-world.

held.title: Corey Fah Does Social Mobility
held.reason: genre question: surreal literary fable about class with UFOs, mutants and wormholes (NYT, Guardian). SF, fabulation, or out of scope?

held.title: Looking Glass Sound
held.reason: genre question: horror/metafiction about a writer, a 1989 Maine summer and a serial killer, blurring reality and fiction (PW, Paste). SFF at all?

held.title: Metronome
held.reason: leaf question: near-future dystopia, a couple exiled to a remote island by an authoritarian government (Guardian x2). Only Orwellianesque fits, and that is the last-resort leaf.

held.title: Sleeping Worlds Have No Memory
held.reason: genre question: Kirkus calls it 'fantasy and SF'; a disgraced royal minister, compared to The Vanished Birds (Locus). Needs a read on which side it falls.

held.title: The Anomaly
held.reason: leaf question: a jet comes out of a storm duplicated with all its passengers, and the world weighs the simulation hypothesis (NYT, Telegraph). Present-day literary SF; no leaf covers it cleanly.

held.title: The Secret Market of the Dead
held.reason: leaf question: folkloric historical fantasy in a fictional Neapolitan town in 1747 (PW, Library Journal). Rococo fantasy is 18th-century but courtly; this is a village smithy.

held.title: The Ten Percent Thief
held.reason: leaf question: authoritarian 'meritocratic technocracy' in a future Bengaluru, told as vignettes (PW, Fantasy Hive). Between Huxleyan and Orwellian leaves.

held.title: The Wings Upon Her Back
held.reason: leaf question: science fantasy of a winged warrior in a god-ruled city (Kirkus, Locus). Hard science fantasy vs Planetary romance unclear.
